HensleyRichards

Hardy and Littlewood's two conjectures clash
Proved in Lean, assuming an open conjecturering 1Patterns, admissibility and the Hardy-Littlewood constants

If an admissible pattern packs more offsets into a window than there are primes in a window of that length, Conjecture A (every admissible pattern repeats forever) and Conjecture B (prime counts are subadditive) cannot both hold.

Open conjectures it assumes (never claimed): HL_conjecture_A HL_conjecture_B

Claims (1)

HL_A_and_B_incompatible
proved in Lean, assuming open conjecture(s)
Given a dense enough admissible pattern, Hardy-Littlewood Conjectures A and B cannot both hold.
/-- **The two conjectures are incompatible.** If a nonempty admissible pattern
fits in a window of a given length (at least 2) and has more offsets than
there are primes up to that length, Conjectures A and B cannot both hold. -/
def HL_A_and_B_incompatible : Prop :=
  ∀ (T : Finset Nat) (y : Nat), T.Nonempty → is_admissible T →
    (∀ t ∈ T, t < y) → 2 ≤ y → Nat.primeCounting y < T.card →
      ¬ (HL_conjecture_A ∧ HL_conjecture_B)
Rests on: no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)
Assumes, never claims: HL_conjecture_A HL_conjecture_B
